summary: The case involves a challenge to the seniority fixation of Munsiffs (Batch of 2003) for promotion to Sub-Judge in Jammu & Kashmir, based on reservation roster points versus merit. The High Court had invalidated the gradation list prepared using reservation roster points and directed re-fixation of seniority based on merit. This decision followed prior Supreme Court directions to reconsider the matter. The petitioners, who were benefited under the reservation-based list, challenged the merit-based re-determination. The Supreme Court, affirming merit as the basis for seniority in promotions, upheld the High Court's decision to reframe the seniority list strictly according to merit and ensure affected candidates are eligible for higher judicial service exams if lower-ranked peers are.

final_judgment: The Special Leave Petition was dismissed, and the High Court's judgment directing the reframing of the seniority list based on merit and quashing the impugned gradation list was upheld. The State was directed to ensure candidates disadvantaged by the earlier roster-based list are eligible for higher judicial service examinations if lower-ranked candidates are eligible.
